newsitem.title: USA: Public Storage forms storage joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Public Storage forms storage joint venture.

text.p: Public Storage Inc. said Monday it formed a joint venture with a major state pension fund to develop up to $220 million of self-storage properties nationwide.
The nation's largest owner and operator of self-storage facilities said the venture is expected to develop between 50 and 60 new self-storage facilities over the next three years.
Public Storage did not identify the pension fund and the information was not immediately available.
The development programme is one of the largest implemented by a real estate investment trust to date, it said.
In the deal, the pension fund will contribute about 70 percent, or $154 million, of the total capital to the venture, with Public Storage contributing the remaining $66 million.

Public Storage said the venture was structured off balance sheet to allow the Glendale, Calif.-based company to expand its operations without the dilution of earnings that typically results from the construction and lease-up of new properties.
Public Storage will ultimately have the right to purchase the pension fund's interest in all the developed properties.
Public Storage is one of the nation's five largest real estate investment trusts, with 1,108 properties in 37 states.
